citation.title: Real-time Estimation of the Electron Temperature Profile in DIII-D by Leveraging Neural-Network Surrogate Models
citation.year: unknown (the PDF shows production placeholders; the key's 2023 is unverified)
citation.doi_or_arxiv: unknown. p1 shows the placeholder xxx/xxxx. DOIs in the reference list belong to cited works.

scope_read.limitations: This is a preprint without production metadata. Figure axes are partly unlabeled in the text extraction. The Ti/Te multiplier value is not given.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The model takes Ti as a multiple of Te
claim_checks.source_finding: Ti is assumed to be a scalar multiple of Te. The assumption enters through the electron-ion exchange term.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: In a model-based DIII-D Te observer, ion temperature entered the electron-ion exchange term as a fixed multiple of Te.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a modelling simplification within one heating term. The multiplier is not reported. The paper does not estimate Ti.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Results are offline tests, not real-time operation
claim_checks.source_finding: The observer was run offline on archived DIII-D Thomson data. The authors state that integration into the PCS is in progress and planned for a later campaign.
claim_checks.locator: p1 Abstract; p10 Sec 4.3; p12 Sec 5
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: An extended-Kalman-filter observer combining a Te transport model with neural surrogates was demonstrated offline on DIII-D Thomson data, with real-time integration described as ongoing.
claim_checks.qualification: No observer latency was measured. The 'real-time' in the title is the authors' design goal.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The observer yields smoother profiles consistent with the data and better than the profile fits
claim_checks.source_finding: The evidence is visual agreement with the same Thomson data used as observer input. Q and R were tuned heuristically to look reasonable, and Q_mag was retuned for the second shot. The core-shape comparison against ZIPFIT and a real-time tanh fit is likewise visual.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: The authors reported visually closer agreement with core Thomson data than tanh-based fits for the shots shown.
claim_checks.qualification: Two shots. No quantitative error metric. No independent truth.

input_target_timing.inputs: Measured output y = core Thomson Te interpolated to 4 grid points. Actuator inputs u = line-average ne, P_ec, eight beam powers, Ip (p7 Eq. 24). Equilibrium is prescribed from shot 147634.
input_target_timing.outputs: Estimated Te profile for rho<=0.9; p14 Fig. 9 adds a linear extrapolation to the edge.
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Recursive filter: prediction followed by correction using the current measurement. Executed offline (p8 Eq. 27-28).
input_target_timing.source_diagnostic_as_input: Yes. Thomson data is both the input and the comparison reference.
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: The comparison is to Thomson reports only.

validation.split_unit: not_applicable for the observer. The NubeamNet surrogate used an 80/10/10 split of time slices, with test R2=0.937 (p4 Sec 2.2.1; p5 Fig. 2b).
validation.temporal_order: Sequential filtering in time. No held-out temporal protocol for the observer.
validation.unknowns: Shot independence of the surrogates from the test shots; multiplier and constant values; quantitative accuracy.

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: No observer timing. Surrogate speeds are stated: NubeamNet on the order of ms, MMM on the order of hundreds of ms (p4 Sec 2.2).
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Observer latency, PCS operation, real-time performance.

forbidden_inferences: Do not state that the observer was deployed or ran in real time.
Do not attribute measured observer latency to this paper.
Do not describe Thomson agreement as physical truth.
Do not claim generalization beyond two shots.
Do not claim the paper estimates Ti or ion/impurity CES.
Do not use DOIs from its references as this paper's DOI.
Do not claim the paper is noncausal or that it represents all prior work.
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. It is model-based filtering of a profile from current measurements. Our work is a temporal nowcast of a not-yet-available CES report from BES/ECEI snapshots and past CES reports. Cite it as an example of the physics-plus-surrogate estimation approach, not as a baseline we compared against.
